gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a power station's inverter uses power just by being on. Measured idle draw with AC on is about 27 W on the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, 9.5 W on the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 and 6 W on the Anker SOLIX S2000. If the AC is left on for a 48-hour weekend, the DELTA 3 Max burns about 1.3 kWh of its 2,048 Wh with nothing plugged in. That is the difference between two 700 Wh e-bike charges and one.
standout_why: I compared against the cited dealectric.com/power-station-to-charge-an-ebike-camping page and powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-power-station-for-e-bike/. PowerStationGearLab covers loss percentages (Jackery 0.85, EcoFlow 0.80–0.90, Anker 10–15%), pure sine wave, DC vs AC, charger wattages and Bosch's 32–104°F charging range. It says nothing about idle draw, eco mode or auto-off, and it recommends the DELTA 3 Max for two 720 Wh charges. Dealectric gives inverter efficiency of 82–92% and mentions BLUETTI's ECO auto-off, but no standby wattage. Both ChatGPT answers offered the DELTA 3 Max ($879) as a two-charge option. Neither mentioned idle draw or switching the inverter off between charges.
decides: It confirms the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 as the pick and makes the DELTA 3 Max a weaker two-charge choice. Two Bosch 4A charges take about 11 hours of inverter time (700 Wh ÷ 0.88 ÷ 144 W ≈ 5.5 h each). At 27 W idle, the DELTA 3 Max loses about 300 Wh just to inverter overhead in that time. Its 79% measured efficiency already puts it at about 1,618 Wh at the outlet, against the roughly 1,590 Wh two charges need, so it has almost no margin. The Elite 200 V2 delivered 1,910 Wh in StorageReview's test and idles at 9.5 W (about 105 Wh over the same 11 hours). That leaves room for both charges. The page should tell shoppers to switch AC off between charges or turn on ECO / AC timeout. It should also list idle draw as a column, with the Anker SOLIX S2000 at 6 W as the low-overhead option (its 1,500 W AC is plenty for any e-bike charger).

findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'After a few tests, we calculated the idle consumption at about 27 watts.' The page has no byline or test setup. Arithmetic: 27 W × 48 h = 1,296 Wh, or 63% of the 2,048 Wh rating, if AC stays on all weekend.

findings.label: Measured efficiency
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Review: A Step Forward or a Step Sideways? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab: 'The efficiency came in at 79%.' The load is not stated. Arithmetic: 2,048 × 0.79 ≈ 1,618 Wh at the outlet. Two 700 Wh charges through an 88% charger need 2 × 795 ≈ 1,591 Wh, leaving about 27 Wh.

findings.label: Inverter hours to charge a 700 Wh e-bike twice
findings.source_title: Best Power Station for E-Bike Charging (2026): 5 Picks and the Charges-per-Battery Math (PowerStationGearLab)
findings.note: The 144 W Bosch 4A charger figure is from this page. Arithmetic: 700 ÷ 0.88 ÷ 144 ≈ 5.5 h per charge, ≈ 11 h for two.
